name: Flix
comment: Derived directly from wstein/flix-fork's real lexer (language/ast/TokenKind.scala, language/phase/Lexer.scala), not guessed -- see jetbrains-plugin/README.md's 'TextMate grammar' section for exactly which rules came from where. This is a best-effort static approximation of that lexer for baseline highlighting when the LSP server hasn't (yet) analyzed a file, not a reimplementation of it: it cannot replicate lookahead-based disambiguation (e.g. '->' vs a user-defined operator starting with '-', or the multi-token string-interpolation state machine) with plain regex.

patterns.comment: Doc comment: leads with EXACTLY 3 slashes (Lexer.scala acceptLineOrDocComment -- '////' is a regular line comment, not a doc comment), so this must be tried before #line-comment.
patterns.name: comment.line.triple-slash.flix

block-comment.comment: Block comments nest (Lexer.scala's acceptBlockComment tracks nesting depth); approximated with a self-including begin/end pair, which Oniguruma-based TextMate engines resolve recursively.
block-comment.name: comment.block.flix

patterns.comment: String interpolation ${...} (Lexer.scala acceptStringInterpolation); nested expression contents aren't recursively tokenized here, just delimited.
patterns.name: meta.interpolation.flix

annotations.comment: Lexer.scala acceptAnnotation: '@' followed by letters only, e.g. @Test, @Domesticated.
annotations.name: storage.type.annotation.flix

builtins.comment: Lexer.scala acceptBuiltIn: '%%' followed by uppercase-leading Java-interop names, e.g. %%java.util.ArrayList.
builtins.name: support.function.builtin.flix

patterns.comment: Control-flow-ish keywords (TokenKind.isKeyword entries used for control constructs).
patterns.name: keyword.control.flix

types.comment: TokenKind.NameUppercase: any uppercase-leading identifier. Flix uses this both for types and enum/case constructors, which a static grammar can't tell apart (that needs the parser); both get the same scope.
types.name: entity.name.type.flix

operators.comment: Fixed 2-char operators from TokenKind (=>, ->, <-, ::, :::, :-, ==, !=, <=, >=, <=>, <+>) plus the isUserOp character class ([+\-*<>=!&|^$], any run of 2+); NameMath (unicode U+2200-U+22FF) isn't representable in a JSON regex charclass here and is left unhighlighted.
operators.name: keyword.operator.flix
